note: Site dates for Karnak (Precinct of Amun-Ra). Years BC are negative. Reign dates follow Shaw (ed.), The Oxford History of Ancient Egypt (2000); other chronologies differ by up to about 25 years for the New Kingdom. Survey draft of 22 November 2026: research fills in who, events and links, and checks every date.
owners: the Eleventh Dynasty kings of Thebes, from Intef II (about 2112 to 2063 BC), whose column naming Amun-Ra is the earliest firm evidence of a temple here
the Twelfth and Thirteenth Dynasty kings, with the temple served by Amun's priests (Senusret I built the Middle Kingdom temple)
the Theban kings of the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Dynasties, while the Hyksos ruled the north (little building is known at Karnak in this period)
the New Kingdom pharaohs from Ahmose, with the temple's lands and workers (the Estate of Amun) under the High Priest of Amun
Akhenaten, who built temples to the Aten in east Karnak, had Amun's name cut out and closed the Amun temple
the restored cult under Tutankhamun, Horemheb and the Ramesside kings, with the High Priests of Amun growing ever more powerful
the High Priests of Amun, who ruled Upper Egypt from Thebes while the Twenty-first Dynasty kings ruled the north
the Libyan kings of the Twenty-second and Twenty-third Dynasties, who made their sons High Priests of Amun
the Kushite kings of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty (control of Thebes from about 750 BC, through the God's Wife of Amun), with the Assyrian sack of Thebes in 664 BC
the Saite kings of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty, who took Thebes in 656 BC when Psamtik I's daughter Nitocris was adopted as God's Wife of Amun
the Persian kings (the Twenty-seventh Dynasty)
the last native kings, the Twenty-eighth to Thirtieth Dynasties, then briefly the Persians again
Alexander the Great and then the Ptolemies, the Macedonian kings of Egypt
the Roman emperors; building stopped, and by the fourth century monuments were being taken down; the end of worship is undated
the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) emperors; Christians used parts of the temple as churches
the Islamic rulers of Egypt, from the Arab conquest to the Mamluks; the village of Karnak grew among the ruins
Ottoman Egypt (with the French occupation of 1798 to 1801, and Muhammad Ali's dynasty from 1805), when travellers, collectors and early scholars visited and removed objects

the Egyptian Antiquities Service, founded by Auguste Mariette, with a dedicated Karnak works commission from 1895; French directors led the service until 1952; the Franco-Egyptian Centre (CFEETK) joined from 1967
the Egyptian Antiquities Organisation
the Supreme Council of Antiquities, under the Ministry of Culture
the Ministry of State for Antiquities (later the Ministry of Antiquities), through the Supreme Council of Antiquities
the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, through the Supreme Council of Antiquities, with the CFEETK for research and restoration

things.name: the column of Intef II
things.who: an eight-sided sandstone column inscribed by Intef II, the earliest firm evidence of a temple of Amun-Ra at Karnak

things.name: Senusret I's temple
things.who: commissioned by Senusret I as the first large stone temple of Amun-Ra at Karnak, about 38 metres square

things.name: the White Chapel
things.who: made for Senusret I, probably for his jubilee festival; Amenhotep III later dismantled it and used the blocks as fill in the Third Pylon

things.name: the White Chapel's recovery and rebuilding
things.who: carried out by Henri Chevrier: the first block was found on 16 November 1927 in the Third Pylon, and the chapel was rebuilt in the winter of 1937 to 1938

things.name: Thutmose I's obelisk
things.who: raised by Thutmose I in front of the Fourth Pylon, then the temple's west entrance, as one of a pair of red granite obelisks from Aswan; later lines of text were added by Ramesses IV and Ramesses VI

things.name: Hatshepsut's standing obelisk
things.who: raised by Hatshepsut in her year 16, counted from Thutmose III's accession in 1479 BC (popular sources say about 1457 BC), as one of a pair of rose granite obelisks from Aswan, its texts boasting of seven months' work and electrum tips

things.name: the fallen top of Hatshepsut's second obelisk
things.who: raised by Hatshepsut as the southern partner of her standing obelisk; it fell in ancient times, probably in an earthquake, and only its top, about 11 metres and 90 tonnes, survives

things.name: the Red Chapel
things.who: made for Hatshepsut as a bark shrine for Amun-Ra, begun or finished about her year 17; Thutmose III dismantled it and Amenhotep III buried the blocks in the Third Pylon

things.name: the Akhmenu (Festival Hall of Thutmose III)
things.who: commissioned by Thutmose III after his Year 23, probably to mark his jubilee

things.name: the Temple of Ptah
things.who: commissioned by Thutmose III on the site of an older mud-brick temple

things.name: the Seventh Pylon
things.who: built by Thutmose III in sandstone, 26 metres high, replacing an earlier mud brick pylon; his smiting scene is on the south face

things.name: the Sacred Lake
things.who: dug for Thutmose III, who records digging a new sacred lake (it may have replaced an earlier one further south); later modified by Taharqa; 128 by 83 metres, filled by groundwater

things.name: the Third Pylon
things.who: built by Amenhotep III from the stones of the monuments he tore down, including the White Chapel and the Red Chapel; it is 28 metres tall and its reliefs celebrate his jubilee

things.name: the giant scarab
things.who: carved in the reign of Amenhotep III as the sun-god Khepri, first set up at his mortuary temple on the west bank

things.name: the Great Hypostyle Hall
things.who: begun by Sety I, who built its walls, columns and roof, and finished by Ramesses II, who completed the decoration; later Ramesses IV and Ramesses VI added cartouches to the central columns

things.name: Sety I's battle reliefs
things.who: carved for Sety I on the north outer wall of the Hypostyle Hall, showing his wars in Canaan, Lebanon, Syria and Libya; the Epigraphic Survey of Chicago recorded them in the 1970s and 1980s

things.name: the peace treaty with the Hittites
things.who: agreed by Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III in Ramesses II's Year 21 (some sources say 1258 BC); the Egyptian text is carved on the Cachette Court wall and at the Ramesseum

things.name: the colossus by the Second Pylon
things.who: made for Ramesses II, with his daughter Bent'anta at his feet, and later re-inscribed by Ramesses VI and by the priest-king Pinedjem I (Digital Karnak lists Pinedjem first, but Ramesses VI ruled much earlier)

things.name: Sety II's triple shrine
things.who: built by Sety II as a resting place for the bark boats of Amun, Mut and Khonsu, and later enclosed by Shoshenq I's court

things.name: the Temple of Ramesses III
things.who: built by Ramesses III as a small temple-shaped bark shrine for Amun, Mut and Khonsu

things.name: the Temple of Khonsu
things.who: begun in the reign of Ramesses III using new stone and reused Eighteenth Dynasty blocks; Ramesses XI and the High Priest Herihor built the front; Taharqa added a porch

things.name: the Bubastite Portal and Shoshenq I's relief
things.who: carved for Shoshenq I to record his campaign into Canaan, with about 156 name rings; he is usually identified with the biblical Shishak

things.name: the Kiosk of Taharqa
things.who: built by Taharqa, a Kushite king, as an open colonnade of ten papyrus columns in Shoshenq I's court; only one column still stands

things.name: the First Pylon
things.who: begun by Nectanebo I as the monumental western gate of the temple, and never finished

things.name: the builders' ramp behind the First Pylon
things.who: built of mud brick by Nectanebo I's workmen to raise stone for the First Pylon, and left in place when work stopped

things.name: the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes
things.who: inscribed with the titles of Ramesses II, though their style looks older (Thutmose IV or Amenhotep III), and moved to Karnak by Pinedjem I on one theory; rearranged under Shoshenq I, Taharqa and the Romans

things.name: the quay and its stone embankment
things.who: begun about the time of Shoshenq I and repaired until the fourth century BC; the tribune platform itself is harder to date

things.name: the granite sanctuary of Philip Arrhidaeus
things.who: carved with the name of Philip Arrhidaeus, Alexander the Great's half-brother, as a copy of Thutmose III's shrine for Amun's bark; one scholar suggests Nectanebo II made the shrine and Philip only had it inscribed

things.name: the Lateran obelisk
things.who: begun for Thutmose III and raised by his grandson Thutmose IV after it had lain 35 years

things.name: the Temple of the Hearing Ear
things.who: built by Ramesses II for Amun-Ra who hears prayers, open to ordinary people

things.name: the collapse of eleven Hypostyle columns
things.who: a chain reaction on 3 October 1899 that brought down eleven columns of the northern wing, blamed on weak foundations of small reused blocks in salty groundwater

things.name: the Karnak Cachette
things.who: excavated by Georges Legrain in four seasons (the IFAO study gives 26 December 1903 to July 1907; some sources say 1905), using shadufs to lift water from a pit about 10 to 14 metres deep

things.name: the reopening of the Avenue of Sphinxes
things.who: marked by a televised ceremony in Luxor on 25 November 2021

things.name: Sety II's small obelisk on the quay
things.who: carved in quartzite for Sety II, about 3.5 metres high

things.name: the Nile level records on the quay
things.who: carved by kings of the Twenty-second to Twenty-sixth Dynasties to record the height of each year's flood

things.name: Taharqa's ramp into the river
things.who: built by the Kushite king Taharqa as a paved stone ramp down to the Nile, used for water rituals

things.name: Hakoris's boat chapel
things.who: built by Hakoris outside the old west gate, with an extra wide west door so the god's boat could be carried in from the river

things.name: Nectanebo I's great enclosure wall
things.who: built of mud brick and sandstone, about 21 metres high and 12 metres thick, around the temple of Amun-Ra

things.name: the Avenue of Sphinxes between Karnak and Luxor Temple
things.who: begun under Amenhotep III, according to Mansour Boraik, and given its sandstone paving and most of its sphinxes by Nectanebo I

things.name: Shoshenq I's court (the first court)
things.who: built by Shoshenq I in front of the Second Pylon, around the shrines of Sety II and Ramesses III; its west wall was removed for Nectanebo I's First Pylon

things.name: Shoshenq I's campaign into Canaan
things.who: the campaign recorded on the Bubastite Portal, dated about 925 BC by Kitchen and linked to the Bible's account of Shishak

things.name: the Second Pylon
things.who: built under Horemheb as a new western entrance, with its passage decorated by Ramesses I and recut by Ramesses II, and with talatat blocks from Akhenaten's temples in its core; it nearly fell in 1899 to 1900

things.name: Legrain's rebuilding of the Hypostyle columns
things.who: carried out by Georges Legrain, who took the fallen and damaged columns apart from December 1899, rebuilt the northern half on new foundations and underpinned the southern wing with brick, and recorded the work complete on 15 May 1902

things.name: the cleaning of the Hypostyle columns
things.who: carried out by Egyptian conservators of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, starting in July 2021 with the twelve central columns; in January 2024 the Council reported 95 per cent of the columns done, with their original engravings and colours revealed

things.name: the Fourth Pylon
things.who: built by Thutmose I as the temple's main western gateway, 23.5 metres tall with a sandstone core faced in limestone

things.name: the Wadjet Hall
things.who: begun by Thutmose I as a colonnaded court, remodelled by Hatshepsut with wooden columns and two obelisks, and roofed in stone by Thutmose III

things.name: the re-erection of the top of Hatshepsut's fallen obelisk
things.who: carried out on 9 April 2022 by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities with the Engineering Authority of the Armed Forces, setting the 11 metre, 90 tonne top upright near the Sacred Lake

things.name: Thutmose III's walls round Hatshepsut's obelisks
things.who: built by Thutmose III as a limestone gateway enclosing the lower parts of Hatshepsut's obelisks in the Wadjet Hall, with her cartouches still intact

things.name: the move of the scarab to Karnak
things.who: probably carried out under Taharqa, who is thought to have brought the scarab from Amenhotep III's mortuary temple to the Sacred Lake

things.name: Thutmose III's granite bark shrine
things.who: built by Thutmose III around year 46 of his reign to replace Hatshepsut's Red Chapel; Philip Arrhidaeus's shrine is a copy of it

things.name: the heraldic pillars of Thutmose III
things.who: set up by Thutmose III in front of the sanctuary, a papyrus pillar for Lower Egypt and a lotus pillar for Upper Egypt

things.name: the botanical room of the Akhmenu
things.who: carved for Thutmose III with plants and animals from his campaigns abroad

things.name: the restoration of the Akhmenu's Southern Chapels
things.who: completed by the Franco-Egyptian centre (CFEETK) with the Egyptian antiquities authorities, reported in June 2025

things.name: the gateways of the Temple of Ptah
things.who: added by the Kushite king Shabaqo, the Ptolemies and the Roman emperor Tiberius

things.name: the shipping of the Lateran obelisk to Rome
things.who: ordered by Constantius II, after Constantine I had had it taken to Alexandria

things.name: the re-erection of the Lateran obelisk
things.who: done by Domenico Fontana for Pope Sixtus V, after the obelisk was dug up in 1587 in three pieces

things.name: Nectanebo I's eastern gate
things.who: begun by Nectanebo I as one of four gates finished in his precinct wall (twelve were planned)

things.name: Karnak's main axis
things.who: laid out in Senusret I's reign or earlier; whether it was set on the winter solstice sunrise is disputed

things.name: the Red Chapel's reassembly in the Open Air Museum
things.who: carried out by the Franco-Egyptian centre (CFEETK); the decision dates to 1997 and sources give the work as about 1999 to 2002

things.name: the erasure of Hatshepsut's name and images
things.who: carried out late in Thutmose III's reign, after his year 42; the reason is debated

things.name: the calcite bark shrine of Amenhotep I
things.who: built by Amenhotep I and left unfinished; Thutmose I finished the decoration of the south wall

things.name: the rebuilding of the Amenhotep I shrine in the Open Air Museum
things.who: carried out by Henri Chevrier, reported 'last year' in his report for 1947 to 1948
names: rebuilding of the amenhotep i shrine

things.name: the calcite shrine of Amenhotep II
things.who: inscribed for Amenhotep II; rebuilt in 2005 in the Open Air Museum between copies of Thutmose I's obelisks, and not the same as the Amenhotep I shrine

things.name: Taharqa's edifice by the Sacred Lake
things.who: built by Taharqa on the north side of the Sacred Lake, with a deep well that seems to have served ritual rather than measuring the Nile

things.name: the Aswan High Dam
things.who: built on the Nile, ending the yearly flood and levelling the groundwater that once refreshed the Sacred Lake

things.name: the finding of the Hittite treaty tablets
things.who: dug up at Hattusa (Boğazkale, Turkey) by Hugo Winckler's expedition; two tablets are in Istanbul and one in Berlin

things.name: the burial of the Cachette statues
things.who: buried in one large pit in the Greek and Roman period; no source records why

things.name: the Eighth Pylon
things.who: begun under Hatshepsut as the first surviving pylon of the southern route, 21 metres high; later kings recarved her reliefs

things.name: the Ninth Pylon
things.who: built by Horemheb, 26 metres high, partly filled with blocks from Akhenaten's dismantled temples

things.name: the Tenth Pylon
things.who: begun by Amenhotep III, who finished only its lowest courses, and completed by Horemheb, with a rose granite doorway 15.6 metres high

things.name: the conservation of the Khonsu temple
things.who: carried out by the American Research Center in Egypt with the Egyptian authorities, cleaning painted reliefs in six chapels and re-laying floors; further work followed

things.name: the Temple of Opet
things.who: begun by Nectanebo I (perhaps on an older temple), modified by Ptolemy III, decorated mostly under Ptolemy VIII and finished outside under Augustus; it has crypts including a tomb of Osiris

things.name: the Bab el-Amara gate
things.who: begun as unfinished pylon towers by Nectanebo I and completed as a 21-metre stone gateway by Ptolemy III

things.name: Papyrus Harris I
things.who: a list of temple gifts and property written for Ramesses III, our best account of how much the temple of Amun owned

things.name: Akhenaten's attack on Amun
things.who: Akhenaten's fifth-year change of name and his attack on Amun, whose name was cut out of temples including Karnak

things.name: the Gempaaten temple
things.who: Akhenaten, in east Karnak, from small talatat blocks

things.name: Tutankhamun's Restoration Stela
things.who: Tutankhamun, to record the restoring of the temples after Akhenaten (dated year 4 by some, year 1 by others)

things.name: the Assyrian sack of Thebes
things.who: the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal's sacking of Thebes, which ended Kushite rule (some books give 663 BC)

things.name: the adoption of Nitocris as God's Wife of Amun
things.who: Psamtik I, to put his daughter into the office of God's Wife of Amun and so control Thebes

things.name: the end of worship at Karnak
things.who: a gradual end, not a single event: imperial bans came in the fourth century but no source gives a date for Karnak itself

things.name: the Christian use of Karnak
things.who: Christians who founded churches among the ruins, most famously in the Akhmenu (the century is uncertain)

things.name: Napoleon's Commission des Sciences et des Arts
things.who: the French scholars and artists who accompanied Napoleon's invasion of Egypt and recorded Karnak (their results appeared as the Description de l'Égypte from 1809)

things.name: the Egyptian Antiquities Service
things.who: Auguste Mariette, for the viceroy Said Pasha

things.name: the Franco-Egyptian Centre (CFEETK)
things.who: France's CNRS and Egypt's antiquities authority, to study and restore the Karnak temples

things.name: the World Heritage listing of Ancient Thebes
things.who: UNESCO, as 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (number 87; criteria i, iii and vi)

people.name: Intef II
people.who: a Theban king of the Eleventh Dynasty, whose reign of about 2112 to 2063 BC gives the earliest firm evidence for Amun-Ra's temple at Karnak
events: became king (Shaw, about)
is thought to have raised a small temple with a columned portico for Amun-Ra at Karnak (about)
died after reigning nearly fifty years (about)

people.name: Senusret I
people.who: the Twelfth Dynasty king (co-ruler with his father from about 1965 BC, sole king about 1956 to 1911 BC in Shaw's chronology; 1971 to 1926 BC in others) who built the first large stone temple of Amun-Ra at Karnak
events: became co-ruler with his father Amenemhat I (about; Shaw)
became sole king (Shaw)
built a limestone temple to Amun-Ra at Karnak (about)
had the White Chapel made (about)
died (Shaw)

people.name: Thutmose I
people.who: an early Eighteenth Dynasty king, Hatshepsut's father, who built the Fourth and Fifth Pylons and raised the older obelisk
events: became king (Shaw)
raised his obelisks in front of the Fourth Pylon (about)
died, after about twelve years as king (Shaw)

people.name: Hatshepsut
people.who: the queen who ruled as pharaoh, Thutmose I's daughter, who raised the tallest standing obelisk in Egypt
events: became regent for the child Thutmose III (Shaw gives 1479 as his accession)
became king (Shaw)
had her obelisks raised in her year 16 (about, counted from 1479)
died (Shaw)
had the Red Chapel begun or finished (about her year 17)

people.name: Thutmose III
people.who: Hatshepsut's nephew and co-ruler, then sole king and great conqueror
events: became king, as a child (Shaw)
began to rule alone, after Hatshepsut's death (Shaw)
won the battle of Megiddo in his Year 23
began the Akhmenu at Karnak
dug the Sacred Lake and built the Seventh Pylon (about; undated within his reign)
his reign reached year 42, after which Hatshepsut's images were erased (about)
replaced Hatshepsut's Red Chapel with a granite shrine (about; year 45 or 46, sources differ)
died (Shaw)

people.name: Amenhotep III
people.who: a wealthy king of the Eighteenth Dynasty, Akhenaten's father, who built the Third Pylon
events: became king (Shaw)
built the Third Pylon (about)
died (Shaw)

people.name: Akhenaten
people.who: the king who turned against Amun in favour of the Aten
events: became king as Amenhotep IV (Shaw)
changed his name to Akhenaten and attacked Amun (his fifth year, about)
moved the court to Akhetaten (Amarna) (about, uncertain)
died (Shaw)

people.name: Tutankhamun
people.who: the boy king who restored Amun's cult
events: became king (Shaw)
had the Restoration Stela made, in year 4 by one reading (about)
died (Shaw)

people.name: Sety I
people.who: the Nineteenth Dynasty king who built most of the Hypostyle Hall and carved his wars on its north wall
events: became king (Shaw)
began the Hypostyle Hall and, in his first year, marched into Canaan and Lebanon, shown on the east half of the north wall
died, leaving the south half of the hall to be decorated by Ramesses II

people.name: Ramesses II
people.who: the long-reigning Nineteenth Dynasty king who finished the Hypostyle Hall
events: became king (Shaw)
began finishing the Hypostyle Hall's decoration, in sunk relief (the Memphis project says within his first two years)
agreed a peace treaty with the Hittite king Hattusili III (his Year 21)
built the temple of Amun-Ra who hears prayers at Karnak (about)
died after reigning 66 years (Shaw)

people.name: Sety II
people.who: a late Nineteenth Dynasty king who built the triple bark shrine in the forecourt
events: became king (Shaw)
began building a triple bark shrine at Karnak (finished by about 1194 BC)
died, ending a reign of about six years (Shaw)

people.name: Ramesses III
people.who: the last great warrior king of the New Kingdom, who built a small temple at Karnak and the Temple of Khonsu
events: became king (Shaw)
began his bark temple in the forecourt and the Temple of Khonsu at Karnak
began the Temple of Khonsu (a mid-reign marker; the year is not known)
died, ending a reign of about 31 years (Shaw)

people.name: Pinedjem I
people.who: a High Priest of Amun who ruled Thebes as king, and who had his name cut on the colossus of Ramesses II at the Second Pylon
events: became High Priest of Amun (about)
took royal titles in Upper Egypt (about; sources vary)

people.name: Shoshenq I
people.who: the Libyan founder of the Twenty-second Dynasty, usually identified with the biblical Shishak
events: became king (Shaw)
led a campaign into Canaan, recorded on the Bubastite Portal
opened a new sandstone quarry for his Karnak building (stela dated to his year 21)
died, after about 21 years as king (Shaw)

people.name: Taharqa
people.who: a Kushite (Nubian) king of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, named in the Bible as Tirhakah
events: named in the Bible (2 Kings 19:9) as king of Kush when Assyria threatened Jerusalem, though he did not become king until about 690 BC
became king (Shaw)
built the kiosk of ten columns in the Karnak forecourt
died, ending a reign of about 26 years (Shaw)

people.name: Nectanebo I
people.who: a Thirtieth Dynasty king, one of the last native pharaohs, who began the First Pylon and the great enclosure wall
events: became king (Shaw)
began the First Pylon and the great enclosure wall (about)
ceased to reign (Shaw)

people.name: Philip Arrhidaeus
people.who: Alexander the Great's half-brother, king in name after Alexander
events: became king, after Alexander the Great died (Shaw)
died (Shaw; Digital Karnak gives 316)

people.name: Georges Legrain
people.who: the French Egyptologist in charge of works at Karnak, who rebuilt the fallen Hypostyle columns
events: took charge of works at Karnak
arrived on 11 December to take down and rebuild the damaged Hypostyle columns
recorded the rebuilding of the northern half of the hall as complete (15 May)
found the Karnak Cachette (26 December)
stopped digging the deepest part of the Cachette pit (14 June)
ended the fourth and last season on the Cachette (July)

people.name: Henri Chevrier
people.who: the French architect who directed the works at Karnak from 1926 to 1954, apart from the Second World War
events: took charge of works at Karnak, succeeding Maurice Pillet
found the first White Chapel block in the Third Pylon (16 November)
finished rebuilding the White Chapel (March)
rebuilt the Amenhotep I shrine in the Open Air Museum (about)
ended his direction of the works

people.name: Ramesses I
people.who: the first king of the Nineteenth Dynasty and Sety I's father, who reigned under two years and left a decorated passage and a small station at the Second Pylon
events: became king (Shaw)
died, after under two years on the throne

people.name: Horemheb
people.who: the last king of the Eighteenth Dynasty, a former general, who built the Second, Ninth and Tenth Pylons at Karnak using blocks from Akhenaten's temples
events: became king (Shaw)
died, having built the Second, Ninth and Tenth Pylons at Karnak

people.name: Thutmose IV
people.who: the Eighteenth Dynasty king (reigned 1401 to 1391 BC) who raised his grandfather's obelisk at east Karnak
events: became king
raised the unfinished obelisk of Thutmose III at Karnak (about)

people.name: Constantius II
people.who: the Roman emperor who had the Karnak obelisk set up in the Circus Maximus in 357
events: became emperor after the death of his father Constantine I
visited Rome and had the Karnak obelisk set up in the Circus Maximus

people.name: Domenico Fontana
people.who: the architect of Pope Sixtus V who re-erected the Lateran obelisk
events: raised the Vatican obelisk in St Peter's Square
re-erected the Lateran obelisk

people.name: Amenhotep I
people.who: the second king of the Eighteenth Dynasty, builder of the calcite bark shrine
events: became king (Shaw)

people.name: Pierre Lacau
people.who: the Director General of the Egyptian Antiquities Service who ordered the emptying of the Third Pylon and later co-authored the Red and White Chapel publications (the Red Chapel volumes, 1977–1979, appeared after his death)
events: published the White Chapel with Chevrier (first volume)

people.name: Herihor
people.who: High Priest of Amun under Ramesses XI who took royal titles, and decorated the court of the Khonsu temple

people.name: Ptolemy III Euergetes
people.who: the Ptolemaic king who built the Bab el-Amara gateway and inscribed the crypt of the Temple of Opet
events: became king (Shaw)

people.name: Ptolemy VIII
people.who: the Ptolemaic king under whom most of the Temple of Opet's interior was decorated
events: became king (Shaw)

people.name: Hattusili III
people.who: the Hittite king who made the peace treaty with Ramesses II
events: agreed a peace treaty with Ramesses II (about; Hittite chronology varies)

people.name: Hugo Winckler
people.who: the German Assyriologist who dug up the Hittite archives at Hattusa
events: began excavating Hattusa and found the Hittite treaty tablets

people.name: Gaston Maspero
people.who: the French Egyptologist who led the Egyptian Antiquities Service and wrote about Legrain's dig as 'fishing for statues'
events: wrote that seven hundred stone monuments had been brought out of the Karnak pit

people.name: the God's Wives of Amun
people.who: the royal priestesses who served Amun and, from the Kushite period, held Thebes for their families
events: Kushite kings begin to put their daughters in the office (about)
Nitocris, daughter of Psamtik I, adopted as God's Wife

people.name: Auguste Mariette
people.who: the French Egyptologist who founded Egypt's Antiquities Service
events: appointed head of the new Egyptian Antiquities Service
